title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Paying Withdrawals and the Per-Cycle Allowance
content:
Money leaving a Savings & Money Market Accounts product, whether as cash, a transfer, an ACH debit, a money market check, an outgoing wire or an overdraft protection transfer into checking, is paid under the rules below. They decide whether the item is paid at all, whether it uses up the cycle's allowance, and which charges it brings.

## Paying a withdrawal

- Only an account in active or dormant status pays withdrawals; the status on the bank's records decides.
- The account balance can never become negative. A withdrawal is paid only if it is no larger than the current balance; one that would push the balance under zero is refused and never posts. An overdraft protection transfer is the one exception to this test on the savings side, because under the Personal Checking rules such a transfer is made only where the savings balance can cover it entirely.
- Each daily ceiling resets with the calendar day as kept in Eastern Time. ATM cash is paid only on a tier with ATM card access, and only within the tier's daily ATM figure. Transfers out through online banking or the mobile app are paid only within the tier's daily transfer figure. Money market checks are paid only on a tier that offers check writing. A request past any of these ceilings is refused and never posts.

## Counting against the allowance

- Cash taken in person at a branch or from an ATM never counts.
- Any other withdrawal counts if its channel is on the tier's list of counted channels. An overdraft protection transfer counts if the tier says such transfers count.
- The count runs over the statement cycle, meaning the days from the day after the previous cycle closing date up to and including the closing date, taken by posted date, in the order the withdrawals posted.

## Excess withdrawal fee

- Each counted withdrawal past the tier's free allowance brings one excess withdrawal fee at the tier's rate, recorded against that particular withdrawal.
- Once the excess fees charged in the cycle reach the tier's per-cycle maximum, further counted withdrawals in that cycle are paid with no fee.
- A tier with an unlimited allowance never charges this fee.
- No withdrawal ever carries more than one excess withdrawal fee; the fees already recorded against it on the ledger show whether it has one.
- The tier that applies is the tier the account was on the day the withdrawal posted.

## Wire charges

An outgoing wire also brings the tier's outgoing wire fee, and a wire credited to the account brings the tier's incoming wire fee. A tier figure of 0.00 means no charge posts.

## Worked count (hypothetical tier: 6 free counted withdrawals, at most 6 excess fees a cycle)

In one cycle the account makes one branch cash withdrawal and fourteen counted withdrawals.

| Counted withdrawals, in posting order | Treatment |
|---|---|
| 1st to 6th | within the free allowance, no fee |
| 7th to 12th | one excess fee each, six fees in all |
| 13th and 14th | paid without a fee, the per-cycle maximum having been reached |

The branch withdrawal is left out of the count altogether.

## Points of judgement

**Can a withdrawal overdraw a dormant account?** No. Dormant accounts pay withdrawals, but never beyond the balance.

**The account changed tier mid-cycle. Which allowance figures apply to a withdrawal?** Those of the tier in force on the day that withdrawal posted.
